subject: Geofence provenance and erasure process — DPA Q&A
messages:
From: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme-corp.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geofence provenance and erasure process — DPA Q&A
Attachments: Acme_DPA_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Hi Mateo / Laura,

Thanks for taking this call earlier. We reviewed the draft DPA and had a few targeted questions about how Redwood handles geofence provenance and the operational evidence you can provide when we request deletion proofs. High-level items we need clarified: 

- When a tenant requests deletion, what exact artifacts are produced (tombstone logs, snapshot IDs, object metadata, KMS event IDs)?
- If backups/snapshots exist in a cross-border cold zone, do you perform on-disk sanitization in-country or do you rotate/expire keys to render backups unreadable? We need the legal and operational distinction spelled out for our Data Protection Officer.
- How do you demonstrate chain-of-custody for a single-customer erasure request? Example: customer X requests deletion at T0, then audit wants evidence at T0+30 days.

Attached is a short spreadsheet with our questions (Acme_DPA_questions.xlsx). Can you reply with a concise playbook and indicate which items you can commit to in the DPA and which require a technical addendum / runbook?

Also copied our legal mailbox for awareness.

Thanks,

Alice Jensen
Director, Security & Privacy
Acme Corp

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geofence provenance and erasure process — DPA Q&A

Alice — thanks for the clear list and the spreadsheet. I pulled together an initial summary below; Laura and Priyom will add the operational details and the playbook PDF. Short answers first so you can take them to your DPO: 

1) Artifacts produced on customer-initiated erasure: tombstone event (internal ID + timestamp), deletion confirmation record (requester, operator, method), object manifest showing removed object keys, and a signed log entry referencing the KMS key rotation event when applicable. We can provide these artifacts as JSON manifests and a signed checksum over the manifest.

2) Backups/snapshots in cross-border cold storage: we support two modes depending on contract: (a) key-rotation-based crypto-sanitization where we rotate/expire the KMS key for a tenant snapshot (this avoids physical re-write but is effective), or (b) scheduled rekey-and-delete which performs an on-disk purge when the customer has an onshore-backup requirement. We'll note both options in the DPA appendix.

3) Chain-of-custody: we create a compact evidence bundle (manifest + signed log + retention policy id + operator audit trail) per erasure request to support future audits. The bundle includes references to snapshot IDs and attestations from our backup provider when applicable.

I'll let Laura drop the playbook and Priyom confirm SLA and runbook items. For anything we mark as an operational addendum we'll propose a separate runbook locked behind a non-disclosure addendum.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme-corp.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geofence provenance and erasure process — DPA Q&A

Hi Alice — adding operational specifics you asked for. Quick bullets below; I'll attach the playbook later today.

- Tombstone logs: retained for 90 days by default in the control plane; each tombstone includes object key, tenant id, deletion method (API/console/ops), and operator id. We can extend TTL for audit purposes if you need a longer retention window for proof-of-deletion.
- Snapshots/backups: our default is multi-zone snapshots that may include regions outside the primary residency. For customers requiring onshore-only backups we offer an onshore-only snapshot option (additional fee). Otherwise, we recommend crypto-sanitization via KMS rotation as the operational control.
- Evidence format: manifests are delivered as gzipped JSON with SHA256 manifest checksum and a signed attest over the checksum (platform signing key). We can also provide a CSV summary if that suits your auditor.

Open question for Acme: do you need physical overwrite evidence (ATA) or does cryptographic rendering unreadable satisfy your compliance? If you need ATA-level proofs we'll need to scope an onshore rewrite window and a limited SLA impact.

Laura Bennett
Head of Product, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 8 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geofence provenance and erasure process — DPA Q&A
Attachments: geofence_playbook_v2.pdf; dpa_changes_redline.docx

Alice / team — attaching the operational playbook and a suggested DPA redline document that maps our commitments to each artifact. Highlights from the playbook: 

- Step-by-step erasure flow (API call -> tombstone -> background purge -> KMS rotation -> manifest generation).
- Expected timelines: ephemeral cache cleared within 30s, primary object purge within 24 hours, snapshots crypto-sanitized within 72 hours or scheduled for onshore purge within 14 days if you select that option.
- Audit bundle contents and retention (we keep the signed manifest for 12 months by default; we can extend to 36 months on commercial terms).

Redline doc: the DPA redline flags two clauses we recommend updating: (1) "destruction" definition to allow crypto-sanitization as a recognized destruction mechanism, and (2) an appendix that enumerates the proof artifacts (manifest, signed log, KMS rotation event id).

Links: DocuSign envelope is ready here: https://app.docusign.com/00123/ACME-DPA-12345

If this looks good, I propose we: (a) accept the redline for the appendix and commit to the 72-hour crypto-sanitization SLA, (b) provide an operational runbook under NDA for ATA-level onshore re-writes.

—Priyom
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme-corp.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geofence provenance and erasure process — DPA Q&A
Attachments: docusign_ACME_DPA_12345.pdf

Thanks everyone — this is exactly the level of detail our DPO wanted. A few quick confirmations before we sign: 

- We agree to accept crypto-sanitization as an acceptable destruction mechanism provided you (a) provide the signed manifest and (b) include the KMS rotation event id in the evidence bundle.
- Acme will take the 72-hour crypto-sanitization SLA for standard accounts. We reserve the right to request an onshore physical rewrite for specific regulated data sets; please outline cost estimates for that option in the runbook.

I'll sign the updated DPA via DocuSign (attached) and return with any final redlines on the appendix. Please also send the CSV summary export for our auditor format.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alice Jensen
Director, Security & Privacy
Acme Corp
